summary: Olivia Chow's public Instagram positions on the small business economy center on supporting local small businesses, creating jobs (especially for young people), and expanding training and apprenticeships. Chow has pledged to fix CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty for small businesses (CthUWn7ADCq). Chow frames small business support as a tool to fight unemployment (mGBcU_OtEi), backs community land trusts as a way for local businesses to thrive (CtPVCP5gBX9), and advocates affordability for artists and the arts sector (CtzvsM3gu6l, CrY6z-PJU2k). Chow has met with taxi drivers about industry fairness (CrqpZEkgbe7) and previously supported a $15/hour federal minimum wage (8qjgVJutDR). Earlier campaign material emphasized job-creation platforms and apprenticeship expansion modeled on the Orlando Training Centre (sx04g1utNg, mGBcU_OtEi).

key_positions.stance: Supports small businesses as a means of fighting unemployment and creating local jobs
Supports fixing CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and reducing burdensome processes
Supports expanding training and apprenticeships, citing the Orlando Training Centre as a model
Supports community land trusts as a foundation for strong local economies
Supports affordability for artists and recognizes arts and film as important to Toronto's economy
Supports fairness in the taxi industry
Opposed relocating 5,000 jobs out of Toronto

key_actions.action: Released the first planks of a job creation and business platform focused on supporting small businesses (March 2014)
Toured the Orlando Training Centre as a model for expanding training and apprenticeships (September 2014)
Publicly questioned John Tory about relocating 5,000 jobs out of Toronto (September 2014)
Met with taxi drivers from across Toronto to discuss fairness in their industry (April 2023)
Pledged as mayor to fix CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating certainty (June 2023)
